goal: A new contributor can install, test, package and maintain ThesisForge, while a reviewer can audit the completed development evidence and SpecNav handoff.
non_goals: Do not publish packages, select a project license or make legal conclusions.
Do not change accepted Parser, Domain, Validator, Compiler, RenderPlan or DOCX behavior.
Do not add Markdown syntax, Template Model fields, UI, backend, cloud or AI behavior.
Do not start six-domain verification, archive or release before the development handoff passes.
expected_evidence: Focused distribution build and installed-wheel regression
Wheel and sdist content inventory with hashes
Temporary no-index/no-deps prefix installation outside the checkout without changing the parent editable package
Offline installed inspect, validate and build using bundled templates
Full pytest, Ruff, pip check, package build, strict OpenSpec and git diff checks
Complete task report, review, ledger, drift and validation artifact audit
Independent spec review and independent quality review
unsafe_assumptions: Editable installation proves a wheel works.
A successful wheel build proves bundled templates and console metadata.
Repository-local CLI execution proves installation independence.
A dependency-resolving pip install proves offline artifact operation.
Existing reports prove current commands still pass.
A locally buildable artifact is legally ready for public publication.
stop_condition: Stop if work changes accepted product behavior, requires network during post-install verification, leaves package/docs/evidence inconsistent, receives a needs-fix review, or the owning SpecNav handoff contract is not ok:true.
